title: OpenAI or Google ends flat-rate flagship access on its $20 tier by Q1 2027
body: Anthropic has reversed its plan to pull Claude Fable 5 out of subscriptions entirely and sell it only per-token: beginning July 20 the model stays included in Max and Team Premium at 50% of limits. The reversal is narrower than the headline reads. Pro and Team Standard subscribers get no inclusion at all — they receive a one-time $100 usage credit, after which continued Fable 5 use bills at API rates — and because Max plans start in the $100-$200 per month range, the practical effect is that the roughly $20-a-month tier loses flat-rate access to the frontier model altogether. The arithmetic behind the concession is thinner still: the underlying weekly limits are themselves being cut by about a third on the same date, so the 50% allowance applies to a smaller base, and the temporary boost to Claude Code weekly rate limits expires alongside it. What makes this generalizable rather than company-specific is the stated reasoning. Anthropic framed the move around Fable demand being hard to manage and frustrating to users, while acknowledging OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol as delivering comparable performance at a fraction of the cost. That is a margin problem rather than a capacity problem, and every lab selling an unmetered consumer subscription against a cheaper rival — with an open-weight floor rising underneath both — faces the same arithmetic on the same schedule. The prediction is that the flat-rate frontier subscription does not survive as an industry norm at the entry price point: by Q1 2027, either OpenAI or Google stops including its newest flagship model at flat rate on its roughly $20-a-month consumer tier, gating it instead behind a usage credit, metered per-token billing, or a higher-priced plan. One lab repricing its entry tier reads as a company-specific correction; a second doing it is what establishes that $20 a month no longer buys unmetered access to the frontier.

reasoning.because: Anthropic keeps Fable 5 in Max and Team Premium at 50% of limits but drops Pro to a one-time credit
reasoning.given: GPT-5.6 Sol matches Fable 5 at a fraction of the cost, with open-weight models pressing from below
reasoning.so_that: OpenAI or Google stops including its newest flagship at flat rate on the ~$20 tier, gating it behind credits
reasoning.landing: by Q1 2027; OpenAI or Google gates its newest flagship off the $20 tier
reasoning.plain_language: Anthropic's best model just left its cheap plan. Expect OpenAI or Google to follow, so twenty dollars a month stops buying the newest model.

summary: Anthropic keeps Claude Fable 5 in Max and Team Premium at 50% of limits from July 20, while Pro and Team Standard get a one-time $100 credit and then API rates — so the $20 tier loses flat-rate frontier access. OpenAI or Google is predicted to do the same on its own $20 tier by Q1 2027.
